gen-gf-gugi-gf-miriam-libre: Bold, open-cut letters with a wiry text face underneath. Gugi does its best work up top, lowercase nearly as high as its capitals; Miriam Libre does its best below, with a wire-like line and generous s bends.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-mochiy-pop-p-one: Open-cut curves meet generously spaced, swell-free letters. Gugi earns its keep in big, short headings where its lowercase nearly reaches the capitals, and Mochiy Pop P One follows with wide gaps between every letter.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-brahmi: Uniform strokes up top, open-ended curves below. Line after line, Noto Sans Brahmi reads smoothly, its high mean line and open curve endings letting the text move along while Gugi stays in the heading.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-tai-le: Noto Sans Tai Le reads gently, its strokes tapering off before they touch. Gugi cuts its letters at a single depth, so the text underneath, with barely any step down from capitals, moves through paragraphs without snagging.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-ugaritic: Smooth, bold curves with no swelling where they meet the stems. Noto Sans Ugaritic does the quieter job, keeping capitals and lowercase close in height with open letter mouths, while Gugi handles the loud, display work.
gen-gf-love-ya-like-a-sister-gf-noto-san: Love Ya Like A Sister is expressive, with terminals pointing outward. Read at length, the heading feels like following a single thread, while Noto Sans Cherokee adds short stalks and a wide-mouthed e underneath.

Love Ya Like A Sister draws round letters like bent wire. What stands out is the hand-off to Noto Sans Mro, whose dense-looking words and large letter entrances give the heading's quiet, level beat something to lean on.
Noto Sans Tai Viet keeps its ascenders short and pulls its terminals back from where each curve would close, staying approachable throughout. Love Ya Like A Sister earns its place big and brief.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-stack-sans-text: Stack Sans Text draws a marker-like line with curve endings held apart. Gugi does its boldest, most distinctive work up top, while the body font's big-bodied lowercase handles the quieter text.
gen-gf-offside-gf-noto-sans-batak: Wide-tracked curves that refuse to close, quietly level. Offside stretches out untapered up top, whereas Noto Sans Batak brings a towering x-height and an e that never squeezes shut.
